subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin own native Slack token rotation now, and where should client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and adopted at runtime?
rationale: The request changes persistent credential storage and active Slack authorization; automation should not choose the permanent storage, refresh, redaction, and recovery model for rotating OAuth material.

options.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep static Slack token support and document external or manual rotation until maintainers are ready to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Wait for generic rotating credentials
options.body: Defer Slack-specific work until OpenClaw has a shared plugin credential refresh and storage API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled Slack setup/runtime and credential-surface history for this security/product choice.
